---
title: "About"
---

I have been a doctoral researcher at the Endowed Chair of Procurement (Prof. Dr. Christoph Bode) at the Business School of the University of Mannheim since September 2026.

I studied economics at the University of Mannheim, completing both a B.Sc. and a M.Sc. in Economics, with exchange semesters at the University of Edinburgh and at the Solvay Brussels School of Economics and Management in Brussels. In my master's thesis I examined how global supply chain bottlenecks transmit to industrial production and producer prices in Germany and the United States. The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung supported my studies with a scholarship in recognition of academic achievement and voluntary engagement.

I worked in empirical economic research throughout my studies. At the Chair of Economic Policy (Prof. Dr. Hans Peter Grüner) at the University of Mannheim, I supported research on mechanism design in asymmetric electricity networks. At ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research, in the Research Unit Pensions and Sustainable Financial Markets, I worked on macroeconomic forecasting, geopolitical risk analysis, and the empirical validation of the ZEW indices.

I also gained practical experience at the interface of corporate finance and procurement. At STATEC Bühnentechnik GmbH, I supported an export financing transaction and worked on improving payment flows and reducing associated risk. Before that, I worked at Russell Reynolds Associates in Executive Search and Board Services.
